At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

How do you spark joy in hundreds of millions of people? It starts with a vision - that technology can give voice to stories around the world. In delivering those much-loved stories, Netflix is responsible for a significant portion of global internet traffic.

To steward that responsibility, we work collaboratively with ISPs to deploy Open Connect, Netflix’s Content Delivery Network (CDN), which delivers 100% of Netflix's viewing traffic.  Our team’s mission is to support that delivery by providing an automation and tooling platform that supports the internal operations and external partnerships needed to provide a fantastic viewing experience for all Netflix members.  We are looking for a talented software engineer specializing in infrastructure to join us on that mission.

The Role

You will be charged with handling impactful availability, scalability, and usability challenges and must self-define optimal ways to configure, manage, and observe our growing Open Connect platform. Our platform is a fundamental building block to our streaming initiatives - providing critical solutions for one of the world’s largest CDNs and empowering stakeholders to operate the CDN more efficiently and reliably. In this position, you will have the opportunity to work in a wide variety of areas, such as:

• Implementing microservices to enable analytics, insights, discovery, and visualizations

• Designing orchestration to manage many thousands of globally distributed appliances and devices

• Building data models and APIs to help manage and maintain our fleet

• Understanding the breadth of our multi-tenant platform, creating solutions which can be leveraged across multiple domains - including networking, video, and gaming

You Are

• Someone who likes to work hands-on and self-direct in a fast-paced environment that gives you great freedom and responsibility

• Able to see beyond immediate specifications, can summarize requirements, and architect forward-looking solutions that cross multiple applications

• Capable of working in a highly-collaborative environment alongside your teammates, engineers, Partner Engagement Managers, project managers, and operations teams

• Articulate in communicating opportunities for continuous improvements to existing systems with a clear understanding of the impact on the business.

• Always striving to develop and deploy in measured increments while taking responsibility for the quality of your work.

Required Skills

• 5+ years of expertise in Java, or similar object-oriented language, with confidence and experience in debugging and problem-solving skills

• Deep understanding of cloud architecture and application deployment

• Ability to build and support highly scalable, robust, and fault-tolerant services

• Experience designing, implementing, and debugging systems that interact with large-sized data sets

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Bonus Skills

• Knowledge of CDN architectures and networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, BGP, DNS)

• Experience with multiple data stores and streaming services such as MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch, Cassandra, Kafka, or Redis

• Familiarity with GraphQL or related graph modeling and querying concepts

• Hands-on Big Data experience using Hive, Pig, Hadoop, or similar

• Understanding of front-end technologies including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, WebSockets

About the Compute group:

Netflix’s Compute group owns our internet-scale cloud footprint. We constantly innovate to increase fleet-wide agility, efficiency, and reliability of this infrastructure. We build, operate, and maintain Compute services so that Netflix developers can rely on foundational building blocks that enable a “set it and forget it” approach to achieving scalability and cost efficiency. We are responsible for one of the largest Cloud Compute footprints built on AWS, and constantly seeking to push boundaries through innovation to delight hundreds of millions of Netflix users daily.

About the Role:

We are seeking an experienced staff engineer to drive the Compute Runtime team’s charter, guide the team's engineering work, and break new ground through hands-on innovation on the hardest technical challenges. You will be part of the team of engineers responsible for the runtime portion of our Cloud Compute group. The team is responsible for enabling containers to run on our compute nodes as efficiently and reliably as possible. The team owns the Kubernetes data plane software; the container runtime; the way we download and run containers; and the underlying compute node’s operating system. The team partners with many other teams within Netflix to ensure we stay ahead of the business's needs and enable other teams to innovate on top of our platform.

You will be amongst the stunning set of engineers who tackle some of the largest Cloud Compute challenges in the industry. We are moving quickly to support critical business initiatives. You will own key pieces of the Cloud Compute infrastructure and be able to directly trace your work to meaningful business impact, all while working on extremely high-scale systems only found at a handful of companies.

Some examples of the team’s work can be found in tech blogs on “noisy neighbor” detection and mount lock contention.

What you will do:

• Deliver compute platform capabilities and drive adoption across Netflix with a focus on engineering excellence, decisive execution, a spirit of bold experimentation, and tight alignment with business context.

• You are an expert in building scalable and extensible compute platforms, and even better at working with other experts. You form strong cross-functional partnerships driven by trust, embracing a highly aligned and loosely coupled approach with many engineering teams, ensuring our solutions meet their needs while maintaining our focus on agility, scalability, reliability, and efficiency.

• Set the example for operational excellence on the team and across Compute, continuously improving incident response, on-call, and other operational practices.

• Maintain currency on, if not create, industry trends for new architectures, features, and off-the-shelf services; guide the team’s decision-making on incorporating industry trends.

• You recognize industry trends early and stay ahead by developing new architectures, features, and off-the-shelf services, while guiding the team's decisions on when and how to adopt them. Identifying trends matters, but you go further: driven by a passion to learn from and contribute to the open-source world, you keep a pulse on it to shape and forecast the direction of technology.

Desired Skills & Experience:

• A proven track record of architecting and implementing large-scale distributed systems that define and modify infrastructure at 100M+ user scale.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with strong relationship-building ability.

• Passion for technology and the ability to jump into an ambiguous area and break down complex problems.

• Demonstrated technical leadership to empower the team around you and get the most from diverse stakeholders, including product managers, peer engineers across Netflix, and more.

• Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and how to abstract away its complexities.

• Experience with Golang, Java, and/or Python.

• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities effectively.

You will be successful in this role if:

• You enjoy operating in an environment where there are rarely obvious choices, and decision-making requires balancing correctness, speed, and uncertainty. You have opinions but are also open to strong feedback.

• You are able to execute strategically in the short term while thinking long term.

• Have the ability to define and self-manage cross-functional projects fueled by ambiguous questions.

• You take pride in your work, and the work your team delivers, and you always think at a team and business level. You bring an uncomfortably exciting mindset and are comfortable with risk in pursuit of the exceptional.

Netflix Cloud is the infrastructure every Netflix service runs on. The Ads Forecasting team builds the predictive foundation of the Netflix ads business — the models that tell us, before a campaign ever runs, how much inventory is available and how a campaign will deliver. We forecast supply and demand across audiences, ad products, and formats, and we predict campaign outcomes such as maximum availability, delivery confidence, reach, and frequency, accounting for the ad-serving optimizations that shape delivery. Our forecasts power media planning, underwriting, budget planning, yield, and the public API.

This is a brand-new, foundational role. You will build the machine learning models that augment our simulation-based engine for predicting campaign delivery — turning a slow, rules-based simulation into fast, accurate, learnable models of how campaigns deliver against real inventory. You'll own the modeling and prototyping end-to-end and partner closely with our ML engineering team to take models to production.

In this role, you will:

•
Build, prototype, and iterate on supervised machine learning models that predict campaign delivery outcomes — delivery risk, reach, frequency, and contention — to replace the current simulation engine.

•
Model demand-side campaign outcomes while incorporating supply-side signals, so the models reason about how well available inventory matches what advertisers are trying to achieve (targeting, frequency caps, contention, pacing).

•
Design rigorous offline and online evaluation frameworks to measure model accuracy, robustness to seasonality and distribution shift, and lift over the simulation baseline.

•
Own feature engineering and contribute to the team's feature store — turning ad-serving logs, campaign attributes, and supply signals into reusable, well-documented features.

•
Prioritize explainability and interpretability: your models' outputs must be defensible to sales and media-planning stakeholders making real booking and underwriting decisions.

•

The Member Experience Client Foundations team (MXCF) is responsible for building the server-driven UI (SDUI) architecture and tooling used to power the member user experience across Netflix’s iOS, Android, TV and Web client streaming applications.

The team is responsible for working closely with our server foundational partners on this SDUI architecture to ensure that we’re building holistic solutions which balance client architectural considerations across all four client platforms, alongside our server partner’s distributed system concerns.
Allowing us to deliver a flexible, scalable SDUI platform on which both our client & server product teams can deliver the innovative member experiences which Netflix sets the industry standard for.

MXCF is a foundational team. We don’t build product experiences directly. We build architecture and tooling which empowers product engineers (our customers), to build great product experiences, efficiently and reliably.
We’re currently working to evolve our SDUI architecture’s capabilities to support:

• A flexible spectrum of server-driven rendering : From coarse-grained control through to fine grained UI control; or none at all, based on product needs.

• Pushing UI updates to the client both for exceedingly high-scale needs (simultaneous concurrent updates for live events), as well user experience updates at lower scale.

• Dynamically modify the UI in response to the user’s session interaction and needs.

• Efficiently support the increasingly wide variety of content types and business verticals (shows, movies, games, ads, live, acquisition) which Netflix supports.

• Integrating generative AI into the ecosystem to increase efficiency for product engineers to utilize the platform.

The Role
This role will be focused on Android, requiring expertise with Android UI architecture and frameworks. However, we believe strong engineering aptitude transcends stacks, and providing the opportunity to explore UI development on other platforms is a unique aspect of this role.

We’re currently building solutions with Kotlin/Compose on Android, and use GraphQL as our shared data access technology. We use Swift on iOS and JavaScript/TypeScript on TV & Web.

In this role you’ll:

• Architect and build maintainable, performant Android client code with effective documentation that can be leveraged by Android developers across Netflix

• Define and drive best practices that ensure consistency, reliability, and simplicity in a high-commit-volume codebase

• Leverage modern technologies such as Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Circuit, and Dagger/Hilt, alongside GraphQL, to deliver scalable, maintainable solutions for our shared SDUI architecture

• Develop code for testability and write automated tests (JVM Unit, Espresso, Paparazzi) to uphold product quality

• Keep a pulse on cutting-edge Android technologies and software engineering practices, modernizing the codebase to accelerate innovation velocity

• Collaborate with cross-functional partners across client and server teams to define and deliver on our framework and architecture vision

• Mentor and grow less-experienced Android engineers

• Influence our framework and architecture roadmaps, and drive forward-looking technical solutions with minimal supervision

• Diverse and inclusive teams are strong teams. We encourage those with varied identities, backgrounds, and experiences to apply. We believe that creating a sense of belonging allows us to be our best selves, which in turn helps us produce our best work. We rely on our unique individual strengths to help each other grow.

• We have a distributed team across the US, while trying to maintain some pacific time overlap. With some teammates working remotely from the east coast, and some co-located in the Los Gatos, CA office. The team is committed to being ‘remote-inclusive’ and believe it’s about the work you do, and the relationships you build. Where you can best do that from is up to you.

People who do well on the team are self-motivated engineers with a passion for building solutions rooted in business and customer needs. Analytical and technical skills form a solid foundation. But more importantly, we look for engineers who understand that there are rarely any absolutes when it comes to technology. The curiosity to engage in discussions about use cases, prioritization and technical challenges with colleagues, while thoughtfully weighing trade-offs across multiple solutions is a skill we value highly. As is the desire to continually learn, grow and help your colleagues do the same.

All of this, so that Netflix members can immerse themselves in the stories they care about, on the devices they love, from whichever part of the world they call home. Without the technology behind it all ever getting in the way.
If this resonates with you, we’d love to talk!

What Sets You Apart:

• You have a deep understanding of the technical landscape of Android development and can introduce new paradigms and practices

• You're comfortable identifying opportunities and driving forward-looking technical solutions or roadmaps with little supervision

• You take a practical approach to problem-solving that considers trade-offs and avoids over-engineering, balancing business, user, and architectural needs

• You have a strong track record of leading projects and delivering results, with excellent project management and estimation skills

• You have an appreciation for diverse perspectives and a collaborative approach to problem-solving.

• You understand that it is really about solving problems. A language, framework or library choice is just a means to an end.

• You've built a track record of weaving GenAI and agentic workflows into your team's engineering practice,  not just using the tools yourself, but changing how the SDLC works for the people around you

What’s Different About Us:
Scale, Impact

Hundreds of Engineers : You’ll be improving UI development velocity for over 100 engineers...
Millions of Users : creating best-in-class streaming UIs used by over 100M users...
Thousands of Devices : across a wide spectrum of devices...
Globally : in almost every country in the world.

We build framework solutions (libraries, architectures, and tools) which are flexible enough to span a variety of product use cases, across a varied client, server and network performance landscape, all while being easy to use for the engineers we support. Collaboration and Communication
It’s not all about the tech. We highly value the skills required to build strong relationships and collaborate effectively.

Responsibility and Ownership
We believe in hiring responsible engineers, providing them with the business context they need, and then freeing them up to own their project’s scope, design, trade-offs, and figure out the implementation details.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a highly technical Product Manager to lead Data Developer & Analytics Experiences within the Analytics Platform & Experiences team.

Your primary mission is to deliver a unified, AI-native experience that spans how practitioners build data assets, build and operate data agents, and orchestrate data workflows at scale. On the Data Developer side, you will own the practitioner “inner loop”; SQL and Python-first code authoring in AI-native IDEs (Cursor, Claude Code, JupyterLab), Python libraries, lifecycle and CLI tooling, data quality tooling, and the developer experience for building data agents that can securely discover, query, and act on data. Analytics engineers, data engineers, and data scientists will be your primary customers, with a focus on making it easier for them to build data assets, orchestrate reliable workflows, and develop data agents. Partnering closely with engineering, design, and data leaders, you will shape product direction and deliver impactful capabilities across developer productivity, workflow orchestration, data quality and observability, and AI-native development.

You will operate with significant autonomy to set strategic direction, define multi-year roadmaps, and make high-leverage tradeoffs across developer productivity, workflow orchestration, reliability and observability, data quality, and AI-native development—including how practitioners build and operate data agents.

What makes this role exciting is the blend of strategic vision and hands-on leadership. You'll maintain a broad portfolio view while selectively diving deep where your expertise makes the biggest difference. •
Set Direction: Develop a compelling long-term vision and strategy for your portfolio, aligning user needs with business objectives and industry trends for the Analytics Experiences.

•
Champion Users: Build deep user understanding and empathy through regular engagement, research, and feedback loops to identify pain points and opportunities.

•
Manage Roadmap: Develop and prioritize initiatives across the portfolio, from IDE-centric inner-loop productivity to centralize Semantic layer and conversational analytics, balancing immediate needs with strategic evolution.

•
Guide Development: Partner with design and engineering to define requirements, create intuitive interfaces, and validate solutions that ensure cohesive user journeys across the platform ecosystem.

•
Support Architecture: Partner with engineering on critical architecture decisions that ensure platform sustainability, scalability, and flexibility while strategically managing technical debt.

Drive Adoption: Create effective rollout strategies and promote new capabilities through targeted communication, education, and roadshows, while providing comprehensive documentation, learning resources, and self-service tools that accelerate adoption and reduce support burden.

Drive Improvement: Define success metrics centered on user delight and productivity gains, and implement tracking to continuously improve platform capabilities through data-informed experiments.

•
Establish Governance: Develop platform standards and processes that balance flexibility with standardization and innovation with stability to maintain quality and consistency, including API design guidelines, versioning policies, and deprecation protocols.

•
Align Stakeholders: Build strategic relationships and foster cross-functional collaboration to drive alignment and create shared ownership of outcomes.

Technical Excellence

•
Expertise: 8+ years of Technical Product Management experience (or equivalent technical role) in complex technical domains. Comfortable discussing technical design trade-offs and system quality attributes with engineering teams.

•
Domain Knowledge: Strong knowledge of modern analytics architectures and data developer tooling — including dbt-based transformation workflows, workflow orchestration and scheduling, and deep familiarity with the practitioner stack: IDEs and notebooks (Cursor, JupyterLab, VS Code), Python/SQL developer tooling, interactive compute environments, and data quality/observability frameworks.

•
Curiosity: Demonstrated passion for Analytics with a pulse on emerging trends. Actively seeks new perspectives and brings fresh thinking to technical challenges. Regularly uses products and observes customers to identify improvement opportunities.

Product Leadership

•
Strategic Vision: Proven track record of managing product portfolios in complex technical domains with clear vision and strategy to maximize portfolio impact. Skilled at connecting business objectives with user needs, balancing quick wins with strategic bets, and making thoughtful trade-offs.

•
Customer Obsession: Deeply understands user needs through continuous engagement. Exceptional at identifying and articulating clear problem statements. Develops innovative solutions with strong product intuition and taste, thinking holistically about end-to-end user experience.

•
Business Acumen: Understands how platform investments drive business outcomes. Articulates the ROI of technical investments in business terms and connects platform capabilities to Netflix's strategic priorities. Balances technical excellence with business pragmatism.

•
Data Driven: Deeply analytical mindset that leverages quantitative and qualitative data to understand user behavior, validate assumptions, and inform product decisions. Builds a metrics-driven culture with clear success metrics to measure impact and drive continuous improvement.

Execution Excellence

The Live Ad Insertions team sits at the intersection of broadcast engineering, streaming infrastructure, and digital advertising. Our mission is to deliver a seamless, high-reliability ad insertion experience across live and linear streams, from primetime tentpole events like the NFL and live sports to 24/7 linear feeds and breaking news. We own the full stack of tools, systems, and operational infrastructure required to trigger, stitch, monitor, and verify ad breaks in real time at scale, without compromising the member experience.

Live advertising is one of the highest-stakes, highest-reward surfaces in CTV. When tens of millions of concurrent viewers are watching a single event, there are no second chances. A break happens once, in real time, and the window to act is measured in seconds. That demands more than reliable systems: it demands proactive observability tooling that can detect anomalies before they surface to members, and the ability to make real-time corrections mid-event when something does go wrong. This team operates with the precision of a broadcast NOC and the velocity of a software startup. We are responsible for the technology that turns a live signal into a monetized ad experience, at scale, millisecond by millisecond.

As an Engineering Manager, You Will

Lead a team of engineers building the real-time infrastructure, tooling, and operational systems for live ad insertion across server-side, client-side, and server-guided delivery models.

•
Own the reliability and operational excellence of ad insertion during 24/7 linear streams and high-stakes live events, including NFL games, live sports, and awards shows.

•
Define the technical roadmap for live ad insertion, including SCTE signal ingestion and validation, ad pod management, manifest stitching, slate handling, and ad decisioning integration.

•
Partner with ad operations, broadcast engineering, content delivery, and ad serving teams to ensure seamless signal-to-slot execution from ingest to client playback.

•
Drive hiring, retention, and development of a high-performing engineering team capable of operating in a demanding live environment.

•
Establish the on-call and incident response culture for live ad systems, setting SLAs and runbooks for break-glass scenarios during high-profile live events.

•
Contextualize your team's larger advertising strategy and translate business priorities into a technically sound, executable plan.

•
Serve as the technical authority in cross-functional discussions on live ad capabilities, representing the team to leadership, partners, and vendors.

Skills and Experience We Are Seeking

Leadership and Cross-Functional Collaboration

•
10+ years of total engineering experience with 3+ years managing software engineering teams in a live media, streaming, or ad tech context.

•
Effective communicator across both technical and business stakeholders, including ad sales, ad operations, broadcast engineering, and executive leadership.

•
Strong track record of hiring and developing senior engineers in competitive talent markets.

•
Ability to operate in a flat, fast-moving organization, balancing long-term architectural investments against immediate operational needs.

•
Proven track record of engineering for high-availability, zero-downtime live events, including building operational tooling for ad ops (e.g., real-time fill rate tracking, signal health visualization, and break monitoring workflows).

•
Strong understanding of ad servers, DSPs, and VAST 4.x/VMAP in live contexts, with a focus on managing strict decisioning latency budgets, timeout handling, tracking event firing, and mitigating the cascading effects of decision failures.

Nice to Haves

•
Vendor Relationships: Experience collaborating with content and distribution partners, including MVPDs, vMVPDs, and broadcast networks, on joint live ad insertion implementations.

•
Streaming Pipelines & Architecture: Deep hands-on experience with live streaming pipelines (from ingest protocols like RTMP, SRT, or TS through to CDN) and ad insertion architectures, including SSAI, CSAI, and SGAI (HLS interstitials/DASH).

Broadcast Standards & Splicing: Expertise in broadcast signaling (SCTE-35, SCTE-104, SCTE-224) and manifest manipulation for ad stitching, alongside familiarity with master control and linear playout systems.

•

This role governs all of it, on the NKP and off, while our technology partner team owns the platform itself.

This is a founding role. You'd be the first to own knowledge governance for Talent, with a genuine greenfield to shape: building the shared taxonomy, the review lifecycle, the cross-GBP forum where these groups align, and the AI-readiness plan that makes this content work with the search tools employees reach for first. This is part strategist, part librarian. You'll also be the bridge between Talent's content and the AI tools that surface it, understanding how search and retrieval consume knowledge and staying ahead of where those tools are heading so our content is built for them rather than catching up. The Language Producer is a Content Localization expert accountable for language and partner health across English-language assets — the main liaison between Netflix and local dubbing, timed-text, and marketing localization vendors, and the execution arm of our partner strategy. This role is the first line of contact for local partners, focused on quality at scale rather than exhaustive title-by-title supervision. Success is measured by the health of the language and partner ecosystem, the role stewards, not by how many titles it personally touches.

This is a 60/40 role: roughly 60% of the time is spent strengthening the local partner ecosystem — vendor relationships, talent pipelines, training, and feedback loops — and 40% is spent on direct, tiered engagement with a curated slate of high-priority titles and assets. Partners are the first line of defense on execution; the Language Producer trains, aligns, and trusts them to meet Netflix’s quality bar, and steps in directly where judgment moves the needle most (in-market popularity, language expansion, new formats, or systemic quality signals). This is a demanding, fast-moving position that requires someone who can hold a strategic, ecosystem-level view while getting as tactical as necessary to deliver content, working across all components of English localization — dubbing, timed text, and marketing — alongside in-territory and cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

PARTNER ECOSYSTEM MANAGEMENT (~60%)

•
Own the local relationship with English dubbing studios, timed-text and DL/PLDL vendors, and talent partners — run recurring tactical syncs and quarterly strategic reviews grounded in performance data, escalating global strategy, vetting, and contract matters to Global Resource Management (GRM).

•
Train, align, and support partners so they can consistently meet Netflix’s quality bar without relying on constant internal review; partners own day-to-day execution, and self-QC and local expertise are the default.

Build and grow talent pipelines and databases for English-language dubbing and audio description; identify casting gaps (mature voices, diverse casting, new AD narrators, niche genres) and design or sponsor initiatives with GRM to close them, monitoring progress against milestones.

Closely monitor union/guild activity, market rates, and the competitive landscape that could influence pricing, capacity, or general market behavior.

•
Act as a local integrator of partner and quality data and escalate critical local issues for visibility, even when the ultimate resolution sits with Legal or Public Policy.

TITLE-LEVEL ENGAGEMENT ACROSS WORKFLOWS (~40%, TIERED)

•
Apply a tiered support model across every asset type: engage directly (“Touch”) on the highest-priority titles for the market — roughly the top tier by in-market popularity, language expansion, or strategic slate — and rely on data and partner escalation (“Analysis”) for the rest of the slate.

•
Import assets (audio and timed text): for Touch titles, own material review (locked cut, context, terminology), creative and operational alignment with partners before work starts (casting, creative approach, scheduling), and creative review of final assets — including a pre-delivery watchdown of secondary audio and targeted timed-text QC — to validate outcomes and extract learnings that improve the wider ecosystem.

•
Same-language and pivot assets (OL forced narratives, SDH, PLDL/DL, English pivot templates): steward partner workflows and standards; align on the creative approach, terminology, and quality expectations for Touch titles; and use QC reports and spot checks to diagnose and address systemic gaps across the rest of the slate.

Define standards of creative excellence and general creative guidelines for the market; conduct risk assessments for special upstream localization requests; and analyze content and language performance trends to address localization challenges in collaboration with Title Producers.

•
Own and maintain language-specific style guides and creative guidelines (Timed Text Style Guides, Audio Description and DL/PLDL Style Guides, Creative Excellence Guidelines), keeping them current, accessible, and reflective of real production workflows.

•
Use guidelines as a primary tool for partner training, performance feedback, and quality interventions, and feed back learnings from title-level work to evolve them with new formats and workflows.

LANGUAGE & PARTNER HEALTH (QUALITY AT SOURCE)

•
Diagnose language health using metrics, QC/TQ signals, and member feedback; translate findings into a market-level strategy — where quality is strong versus where systemic intervention or training is needed.

•
Track vendor performance over time to inform smart routing, training priorities, and vendor-mix decisions, with the goal of reducing reliance on third-party QC as partner quality matures.

•
Stay current on how technology — ASR, machine translation, TQ models, and automation — is reshaping the localization process, and help define “fit-for-purpose” quality standards by format and tier as the company’s strategy develops.

Act as subject matter expert for localization workflows in English, supporting the Dubbing Strategy and Innovation roadmap and Netflix’s tooling ecosystem to drive vendor adoption.

Participate in tests and quality control of lip sync, VO, machine translation, and core asset roll-outs; feed structured feedback back to Strategy & Innovation (S&I) and algorithm teams rather than treating model outputs as a black box.

Initiate, support, and collaborate with cross-functional partners on Inclusion and Diversity initiatives to keep strategy consistent across the organization.

Be sensitive to the local competitive landscape and maintain a working knowledge of localization contracts and local best practices between talent and Netflix’s vendors.

Integrations (APIs, events, batch, and file-based, where necessary).

Identity, entitlements, and access control across HR systems.

Ensure HR data is traceable, auditable, and explainable from original source to reporting and downstream usage.

Embed security, privacy, and regulatory requirements directly into the architecture, including:

Regional data residency and cross‑border data transfer considerations.

Role‑based access controls and least‑privilege principles.

Employee privacy expectations and internal policies.

Partner with Security, Privacy, and Legal to convert these requirements into repeatable technical patterns rather than ad‑hoc process overlays.

Translate business outcomes into solution architectures that are sustainable, maintainable, and aligned with long‑term strategy, not just limited by immediate tool configuration options.

Review solution designs and identify approaches that conflict with the target architecture.

Enable vertical/domain teams to focus on business needs by ensuring the horizontal foundations are robust and well‑defined.

Represent the HR architecture to 3P vendors and partners.

Make explicit, documented decisions on:

Short‑term HR needs versus long‑term ecosystem health and simplification.

Level of customization versus maintainability, scalability, and upgradeability.

Document decisions and rationale and be prepared to revisit them when new evidence emerges.

Identify opportunities to rationalize redundant tools, platforms, and integrations.

Propose and lead decommissioning efforts for low‑value, high‑cost, or overlapping components.

Champion an architectural approach that reduces complexity, improves reliability, and lowers total cost of ownership across the HR technology landscape.

Advanced degree (PhD or Masters) in Computer Science, Statistics, Economics, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.

8+ years of experience with statistics / causal inference in an experimentation context, including designing experiments at scale and diagnosing them when they break.

•
Demonstrated track record of setting standards or building tools that were adopted across multiple teams or an entire organization - not just applying judgment project by project.

•
Deep, practical knowledge of experimentation pitfalls and how to guard against them at a program level: sample ratio mismatches, winner's curse and regression to the mean, false discovery rate across a portfolio of tests, peeking, covariate adjustment, and allocation-vs-analysis-unit mismatches.

Experience translating ambiguous data science pain points into a sequenced product roadmap, including judgment on what a platform should build in, expose as a self-serve primitive, or explicitly not support.

Change Management Practice & Framework

•
Define and own the Finance PMO change management methodology - establishing a scalable, repeatable framework (tools, templates, and standards) that elevates the consistency and quality of change delivery across all PMO-led programs.

Develop and maintain a library of reusable change management artifacts: stakeholder analysis templates, change impact assessment frameworks, communication plan structures, readiness survey toolkits, RACI models, and training design guides.

Act as the internal expert and coach on change management best practices; build change capability across the PMO team and broader Finance organization so that change management becomes a core competency, not a one-off activity.

Benchmark against industry frameworks (e.g., Prosci/ADKAR, Kotter, McKinsey Influence Model) and adapt them pragmatically to Netflix's culture and operating model.

Portfolio Change Management

•
Provide holistic change management strategies across the Finance PMO project portfolio - ensuring that change impacts are assessed, sequenced, and managed at the portfolio level, not just the individual project level.

Lead change management on significant, high-visibility PMO initiatives from end to end: scope change impact assessments, develop and execute communication plans, manage stakeholder engagement, design and oversee training programs, and conduct readiness assessments prior to go-live.

Proactively identify change saturation risks across the portfolio - flagging moments when concurrent programs may overwhelm stakeholder groups - and recommend sequencing or pacing adjustments to protect adoption outcomes.

Partner closely with Finance PMO Senior Program Managers and Program Managers to integrate change management activities into project plans, ensuring change is never treated as an afterthought.

Manage and track change management deliverables across the portfolio; provide regular reporting on change health, adoption progress, and stakeholder sentiment to PMO leadership.

Lead, develop, and retain a team of direct reports; set clear performance expectations, provide consistent coaching, and conduct formal performance management with transparency and care.

Build a culture of high standards - holding the team to rigorous craft while creating the psychological safety needed for iteration and growth.

Manage team capacity across the portfolio; make deliberate prioritization calls when demand exceeds bandwidth and escalate tradeoffs clearly to PMO leadership.

Build change management capability across the broader Finance PMO — coaching program managers and business partners to embed change thinking into their work, extending the team's reach without extending headcount.

Build strong relationships with Finance stakeholders to gain deep understanding and awareness of their unique needs.

Design stakeholder engagement strategies that go beyond information sharing — creating experiences that build genuine understanding, confidence, and commitment to change.

We're looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead this team. This is a small, senior, high-leverage group working at the front edge of a domain that is still being invented — where frameworks turn over in months and the durable bets are not obvious. The hardest part of this job is not the code — it is choosing what to build, and what will still matter once today's tools are gone.

Own the charter and technical direction. Set the platform's technical strategy and roadmap — the agent-specific foundation every agent depends on, and the selective runtimes worth operating directly — and decide where to invest ahead of demand.

Lead and grow a high performing team. Hire, develop, and retain excellent engineers; set a high bar; and create the conditions for a small team to have outsized impact.

•
Make sharp build, adopt, or partner calls. Decide which capabilities the platform owns and which it draws from partner teams, define the interfaces between them, and keep a small team focused on the highest-leverage layer.

•
Turn the new hard problems into primitives. The most durable problems in this space are the ones that let agents get better from their own experience: capturing each run's full reasoning-and-tool-call trajectory as structured, replayable data; turning real-world outcomes into evaluation signal; memory that compounds across runs; and a feedback loop that turns that signal into improved behavior, promoted behind eval gates and safe rollout. Make these first-class platform capabilities with real contracts — so agents built on the platform measurably improve over time, not just scale.

•
Operate as part of the AI Platform leadership team. Set direction alongside peer leaders across the AI Platform and partner orgs, represent the team in senior technical forums, and build the cross-team alignment a foundational platform depends on.

The Content Representation Models team creates a single, unified "language" for Netflix's entire library by developing foundation models that understand everything from video and audio to text and artwork at a semantic level. By treating these powerful embeddings as a core product, we give Netflix the ability to match the right content to the right member, supercharging personalization and helping everyone discover something they'll love.

The team's current areas of focus include:

•
Unified Content Embedding: Merging media-based and metadata-based embedding approaches into a single cohesive model, creating rich semantic representations of all content across video, audio, and text modalities

•
Multimodal and Multi-Granularity Embeddings: Creating embeddings from various content types at different levels of detail, from entire shows down to individual shots and clips

•
Semantic IDs: Developing unique, meaningful identifiers for content that enable more sophisticated retrieval and recommendation

•
Profile and Content Embedding Alignment: Aligning member profile embeddings with content embeddings in the same space to enhance personalization

About the Role

We are looking for a Research Scientist specializing in embeddings and representation learning to investigate how we can enhance content understanding capability in Netflix's foundation models.

How foundation models understand content is one of the most important open research questions for Netflix personalization. Today, our models rely on a mix of metadata, behavioral signals, and media-based representations. The opportunity ahead is to significantly deepen that understanding through approaches like Semantic IDs, continuous pre-training, novel representation learning methods, or other state-of-the-art techniques.

The person in this role will help shape that research direction and bring new ideas to the table. This is an area where the optimal strategy is still being defined, which means there is real room to influence the approach and make a lasting impact on how Netflix's foundation models reason about content.

What makes this role unique:

•
Open research problem with real product impact. Enhancing how foundation models understand content is a crucial and unsolved challenge. Your work will directly improve how 300M+ members discover content.

•
Research that ships. This isn't a pure research lab. Your work will feed into foundation models that power personalization across every Netflix surface. The loop between research and member impact is tight.

•
Bring your own approach. We have hypotheses (Semantic IDs, continuous pre-training, etc.) but we're looking for someone who brings their own perspective and methods to the problem.

•
World-class collaborators. You will work alongside researchers and engineers across content understanding, foundation models, and application teams who are pushing the state of the art in personalization at scale.

Responsibilities

Drive applied research on enhancing content understanding capability in Netflix's foundation models

Conceptualize, design, implement, and validate new approaches to representation learning and content embeddings

•
Explore and apply state-of-the-art AI/ML techniques, including methods for improving how LLMs and foundation models represent and reason about content

•
Develop production-ready solutions and partner with application teams to ensure research translates into member-facing impact

•
Design and run rigorous offline experiments and evaluations to validate new approaches

•
Collaborate with cross-functional teams across content understanding, foundation models, and personalization applications

•
Contribute to the broader research community through publications at top venues

Ph.D. in Computer Science or a related field with a strong publication record in embeddings, representation learning, or a closely related domain

3+ years of research experience with a track record of delivering quality results

Strong software engineering skills in Python (eg, PyTorch /)

Experience in adopting LLM for Recsys. More specifically, building Semantic IDs and ground them in LLMs.

Experience in computer vision or multimodal AI

Industry experience in recommendation systems, search, personalization, or retrieval

Hands-on experience with distributed training

Publications in top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, KDD, RecSys)

The Physical Identity and Access Manager is responsible for overseeing the development, implementation, and management of the company’s physical identity and access management program. This role ensures the security and safety of employees, visitors, and physical assets by managing access control systems and protocols. The Physical Identity and Access Manager will work closely with various departments to ensure compliance with security policies and procedures while providing excellent customer service. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences to apply—even if you don’t meet every qualification listed. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.

•
Set and maintain high standards for the design, configuration, operation, and quality assurance of all physical identity and access management (PIAM) systems and platforms.

•
Develop, implement, and manage physical access control policies and procedures.

•
Manage access rights and permissions for employees, contractors, and visitors.

•
Lead the deployment and integration of advanced technologies (including AI, automation, and biometrics) to enhance and streamline Netflix’s physical security and access control programs.

•
Manage the issuance and revocation of physical and mobile identification credentials.

•
Ensure accurate and up-to-date records of all identity and access data.

•
Collaborate with HR and IT departments to integrate identity management with other systems.

•
Conduct regular audits of access control systems and processes.

•
Collaborate with business partners in HR, Contingent Talent, Workplace, People Tech, and IAM to ensure seamless integration of PIAM solutions within Netflix’s global ecosystem.

•
Shape and support the PIAM technology roadmap in alignment with departmental and organizational goals.

•
Design, implement, and maintain robust processes for collecting and centralizing access logs and physical security data, enabling advanced analysis and visualization of physical security metrics.

•
Review and ensure compliance with data privacy, access control, and physical security requirements.

•
Develop and track metrics to measure the effectiveness and impact of PIAM solutions.

•
Advise teams across the company on PIAM solutions, design, and deployment.

•
Communicate program updates and technical information clearly to all stakeholders.

•
Develop technical documentation, training materials, and best practice guides for cross-functional teams.

Qualifications:

•
10+ years of experience with increasing scope, responsibility, and complexity at a multinational company.

•
Proven experience leading global, cross-functional PIAM or physical security initiatives and collaborating with diverse stakeholders.

•
Strong project management skills, with experience in setting and achieving objectives through OKRs or similar frameworks.

•
Deep understanding of physical access control systems, identity management, and emerging physical security technologies.

•
Up-to-date knowledge of global physical security trends, regulations, and compliance requirements.

•
Creative problem-solver with a passion for innovation and continuous improvement.

•
Experience in the entertainment, technology, or critical infrastructure sectors is highly desirable.

•
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

•
Willingness to run lean with a DIY mentality, take educated risks, and think out of the box.

•
Travel regionally and internationally as required (approximately 25%).

We’re looking for a versatile and engaged Tech Director to join our Internal Game Development team and contribute to our goal of bringing best-in-class games to our members. The Tech Director will partner with cross-disciplinary teams to define and execute high-quality tech direction across a range of projects. This role requires a balance of technical leadership and hands-on implementation, with the ability to manage external partners, support multiple teams simultaneously, and establish scalable engineering practices that elevate the player experience across our games.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on technical leader with deep expertise in Unreal Engine 5 or Unity, game systems, architecture, and cloud technologies, paired with a passion for innovation and player experience. You’ll operate as a key member of our studio leads group, partnering closely with the Game Director, Creative Director, Art Director, and Executive Producer to ensure seamless alignment between product, technology, and creative goals. You’ll set the bar for engineering excellence, drive integration with Netflix’s platform technologies, and champion a culture of experimentation, learning, and collaboration.

You’ll be joining an internal studio with big ambitions, and an obsession to create memorable game moments that leave players telling their own stories for years to come. We’re looking for new teammates who care deeply about the experiences they create and the people they make them with. Those who bias towards action and are energized by the learning that comes with bold experimentation at an agile pace. As a part of Netflix, we strive to hire the best and value integrity, excellence, respect, inclusion, and collaboration.

RESPONSIBILITIES

•
Technology Visionary: Own all technical aspects of the project, from architecture and system design to development processes and technical documentation. Ensure the project’s technical direction is scalable, sustainable, and aligned with our creative vision.

•
Team Builder: Hire, mentor, and lead a world-class engineering team, cultivating an environment focused on innovation, growth, and exceptional development standards.

•
Execution Leader: Oversee technical execution across prototype, production, and live ops. Set and uphold the bar for code quality, performance, and reliability, and optimization.

•
Strategic Partner: Collaborate with studio leads to keep the project aligned with product strategy, and proactively drive course corrections when needed.

•
Platform Integrator: Champion the integration of Netflix’s cloud-gaming platform technologies, ensuring our team is a front-runner for innovation within Netflix.

•
Co-Dev Arbiter: Identify and evaluate potential external co-development partners, ensuring technical compatibility and smooth cooperation.

•
Engineering Backstop: Serve as the final escalation point for all engineering-related challenges, troubleshooting and resolving issues to keep the team moving forward, including deep engine-layer debugging and performance profiling.

•
Process Architect: Continuously refine development processes, tools, and pipelines for optimal efficiency and scalability with a “build and play often” mentality.

•
Cultural Leader: Lead by example, fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performance culture within the engineering team and across the studio.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

•
Brings 10+ years of experience developing and launching high-fidelity games, with recent, deep hands-on expertise in Unreal Engine 5 or Unity and C++.

•
Skilled at profiling and debugging at the engine layer, including diagnosing frame time and memory issues using Unreal’s tools.

•
Expert in building and maintaining modular, scalable frameworks, with hands-on experience managing world partition, level streaming pipelines, asset virtualization, shader compilation, and build/cook systems.

•
Proven track record optimizing CPU, GPU, and memory footprints for constrained environments, as well as evaluating bandwidth and latency constraints to ensure performance and gameplay targets are met.

•
Deep technical expertise across game architecture, gameplay systems, content pipelines, artist workflows, rendering, backend services, and cross-platform development (including Linux).

•
Collaborates closely with art and design teams to balance visual fidelity and performance, and supports live service games through development, launch, and post-launch operations.

•
Familiar with contemporary web technologies (JavaScript, React, etc.) and cloud environments (AWS, GCP, etc.).

•
Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and scale multidisciplinary engineering teams, collaborating effectively with both technical and non-technical leaders.

•
Exceptional communicator, skilled at building trust and alignment across teams and stakeholders.

•
Is self-motivated, curious, and eager to pitch in wherever needed, even outside their core responsibilities.

•
Thrives in fast-paced, evolving environments, navigating change with maturity, empathy, and a bias for action.

LOCATION

•
Los Angeles preferred

•
Will consider remote applicants who are willing to travel for work-related events and work a PST-oriented dev team schedule.

Retail Manager -  Netflix House

Netflix is one of the world's leading entertainment services, with over 300 million paid memberships in over 190 countries enjoying TV series, films and games across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.

Netflix House is a permanent entertainment venue where fans can interact with their favorite Netflix stories through immersive experiences and elevated hospitality. The first two locations will open at King of Prussia in Pennsylvania and Galleria Dallas in 2025. Netflix House is another step in Netflix's commitment to create immersive, in-person experiences for fans around the globe, including NETFLIX BITES Las Vegas, The Queen’s Ball: A Bridgerton Experience; Stranger Things: The Experience; Squid Game: The Experience, now open in New York, Madrid, Sydney and Seoul; and Stranger Things: The First Shadow, now open on London’s West End and coming to Broadway March 28. Netflix has reached 7.5 Million fans across 170 openings in 100 cities and 40 unique formats around the world with an average guest rating of 4.7 out of 5.

As the Retail Manager, you will lead the Fan (guests) and Crew (staff) experience in the retail component of Netflix House. Your responsibilities include oversight of the Retail Associate, Leads, and Crew that are engaging fans, selling merchandise, staffing the main retail space, and smaller pop-up locations while monitoring sales and revenue goals. You will be tasked with overseeing daily staffing plans, hiring, training, and developing the local retail crew. You will partner with our Retail Vendor team, who is the stakeholder in sourcing and purchasing products, ensuring sales revenue is optimized in collaboration with Netflix Corporate strategy. You are an individual who is passionate about sharing Netflix fandom by leading a crew that is set up for success with great training, knowledge, and the right tools to create memorable experiences. The ideal Retail Manager is a communicative leader dedicated to developing and connecting with their team.

This role reports to the Assistant General Manager and is a salaried, on-site role based in King of Prussia, PA.

•
Manage the daily on-site operations and team for the retail store and pop-ups, focusing on sales optimization and fan service informed by revenue targets and budgetary constraints.

•
Partner with Retail Vendor on on-site inventory allocation and replenishment, sales tracking, and overall sales performance.

•
Develop hiring, training, and deployment processes strategies for the retail crew.

•
Optimize ongoing operations to achieve maximum efficiency and best-in-class Fan Service.

•
Work closely with Netflix Corporate resources on operational SOPs, merchandise strategy, and retail trends.

•
Follow the Netflix Corporate visual merchandising strategy in store to ensure a cohesive look across Netflix Houses.

•
Act as a Manager on Duty and Safety on Duty for the operation.

•
Align with the Assistant General Manager and other departments to provide a seamless Fan experience.

•
Promote and foster a mindset of continuous innovation for internal teams and external partners.

•
Demonstrated 5+ years of retail store and team management experience.

•
Strong knowledge of hiring practices and training & development strategies.

•
Strong knowledge of retail trends in the Location Based Entertainment (LBE) industry, preferred.

•
Experience managing direct and indirect teams in an environment that embraces continual learning and change.

Team Overview

The Traffic Engineering team designs, builds, and operates the core infrastructure that manages how traffic flows across Netflix’s cloud and edge environments. Our systems ensure that every member receives a fast, reliable, and high-quality streaming experience, even during massive live events and unexpected spikes in demand. The TMF team is instrumental in driving Netflix’s cloud scalability and resiliency by building robust capabilities for end-to-end traffic management, including region failover, traffic shaping, and predictive scaling. We work closely with Data Science to develop and operationalize predictive models, translating them into actionable strategies for scaling our infrastructure in real time. By automating and optimizing traffic management, we enable Netflix to deliver uninterrupted entertainment to hundreds of millions of members worldwide—making our work critical to Netflix’s reputation, member satisfaction, and continued growth.

Why our work is important

The work of the Traffic Engineering team is critical to Netflix’s ability to deliver a seamless, high-quality streaming experience to hundreds of millions of members worldwide. As Netflix expands into live events and continues to grow its global audience, the demands on our infrastructure for speed, reliability, and scalability have never been higher. Our team ensures that Netflix can handle massive spikes in traffic—such as during live sporting events or global premieres—without interruption or degradation in quality. By building resilient systems for traffic management, automated scaling, and rapid failover, we protect the member experience and uphold Netflix’s reputation for reliability. The innovations and solutions developed by the TMF team directly enable Netflix to push the boundaries of what’s possible in streaming, supporting new business opportunities and ensuring that our members can enjoy their favorite stories anytime, anywhere, without compromise.

This would be your dream job if you enjoy:

• Solving real business needs at a large scale by applying your software engineering and analytical problem-solving skills.

• Architecting and building a robust, scalable, and highly available distributed infrastructure. You enjoy the pursuit of engineering excellence by evangelizing, establishing and iterating on best practices.

• collaborating with multiple teams on creating solutions and supporting solutions with a myriad of sometimes conflicting requirements.

• You are curious and enjoy working on ambiguous problems where the solutions are not (yet) well defined.

Qualifications:

• 7+ years experience in crafting complex, scalable distributed data infrastructure. Experience in traffic is preferred

• Proficiency in Java, Golang, or Python with a solid understanding of multi-threading and memory management

• Able to break down complexity, iterate, and communicate progress to a wide variety of partners and stakeholders.

• Proven track record of developing and maintaining high-impact systems

• Experience building and operating scalable, fault-tolerant, distributed systems

• Automation and orchestration frameworks for scaling and reliability

• Experience in predictive modeling and data pipelines for traffic shaping and scaling

• High Impact - your work will touch every engineer at the company and be crucial for the ongoing success of Netflix.

• Stunning Colleagues - you will be working with other excellent people with diverse perspectives, who value collaboration, working to excel as the “dream team”.

Model Evaluations and Data Curation ("MEDC") forms the flywheel of foundation model development at Netflix. We build the benchmarks, evaluators, and baselines that guide progress on our foundation models, and the data infrastructure that delivers high-quality, reproducible training and evaluation datasets to our AI/ML researchers.

Together, these capabilities create a continuous loop of data → train → evaluate → adapt, driving faster and more confident innovation. Our work is upstream of nearly every AI-powered member experience at Netflix, making our impact unusually broad for a team of this size.

The team has two major areas of focus:

• Data Curation: Selecting, cleaning, and organizing raw data to create the best possible training sets for our models. The more abstractions we can make on the data, the faster we can innovate.

• LLM Evaluations: Providing benchmarks for foundational models and datasets, ensuring confidence and trustworthiness when offering these building blocks to application teams.

About the Role

We are looking for a Software Engineer to build the common infrastructure for data curation at MEDC. Today, data curation work across MEDC and our modeling partners (e.g., semantic and content QA datasets, generative retrieval evals) happens largely in ad-hoc notebooks, with no shared capabilities or standardization. This makes every new curation project slow to launch, hard to discover, and labor-intensive to productionize. You will turn that into a coherent, reusable platform.

This is not a pure data engineering role. The core of the work is using LLMs to transform data, for example turning the Netflix catalog and member signals into question-answer pairs, and then deciding what to keep. That means designing sampling strategies and filtering methods, often based on evaluation models, that maximize data quality, and proving that those choices actually improve downstream models. You will work hand in hand with researchers, so modeling intuition matters as much as engineering skill.

Responsibilities

• Design and build shared data curation infrastructure (reusable components, libraries, and workflows) that replaces ad-hoc notebooks and makes new curation projects fast to launch and easy to productionize

• Build scalable LLM-driven data transformation pipelines that turn raw sources such as the Netflix catalog and metadata into training and evaluation data (e.g., question-answer pairs, synthetic scenarios), using large-scale batch inference with attention to quality and token cost

• Develop sampling strategies (coverage, diversity, difficulty, and balance across content and member segments) for constructing training and evaluation sets

• Develop filtering and quality-control methods, including LLM-as-judge and evaluation-model-based scoring, deduplication, and validation, to maximize data quality

• Partner with researchers to measure how curation choices affect model performance, closing the loop between data quality signals and model outcomes

• Make curated datasets first-class, discoverable artifacts with versioning, explicit lineage, and reproducibility, so teams can find, reuse, and build on each other's work

• Drive adoption of shared curation practices across MEDC and partner modeling teams

What We're Looking For

Must-haves:

• Strong software engineering in Python, with experience building reusable infrastructure, libraries, or frameworks used by other engineers and researchers

• Experience building LLM-driven data generation or transformation pipelines (e.g., synthetic data, structured outputs, batch inference at scale)

• Hands-on experience with data quality methods: sampling strategies, filtering, deduplication, and model-based quality scoring such as LLM-as-judge

• Modeling intuition: an understanding of how data choices affect model behavior, and the ability to design experiments that measure it

• Experience with distributed data processing (e.g., Spark, Ray, or similar)

• Excellent collaboration skills, particularly with researchers, data scientists, and platform teams

Nice-to-haves

• Experience with LLM evaluation systems (must-have for L6)

• Technical leadership across data and evaluation infrastructure; experience setting technical direction for a multi-engineer effort (must-have for L6)

• Experience with human annotation workflows and calibrating LLM judges against human raters

• Experience with pipeline orchestration frameworks (e.g., Metaflow, Airflow, or similar)

At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

The Title and Launch Management (TLM) team is responsible for building and innovating the technology foundations that enable the ingest, setup, launch, and global distribution of all types of entertainment on Netflix—including series, movies, games, ads, live events, trailers, and more. TLM acts as the bridge between the title creation lifecycle and the consumer experience, ensuring that launching titles on Netflix is efficient, flexible, accurate, and scalable. Our team's goal is to make launching titles as seamless as possible, supporting both operational and creative needs across the company.

The Catalog Integration team turns the outputs of many independent content workflows into a coherent catalog that other systems can use. Partner teams create the artwork, language assets, ratings, descriptions, trailers, and other information that surrounds a title; Catalog Integration provides the federated data API and transformation layer that bring those outputs together, connects them into the catalog graph, and transforms them into a consistent view.

We publish the real-time feeds that unblock every downstream, member-facing system — the moment our feeds go out, hundreds of services spring into action to serve that update to members. We invest in proprietary, cutting-edge tooling for data snapshots, recovery, graph-aware rollbacks, fast/override publication lanes, and realtime overrides, so that one bad entry never holds up the rest of the catalog. Our work enables Netflix's cutting edge business bets like Live, Games, and Sports while continuing to deliver the critical data that drives the streaming video content experience.

What you will do

You will lead a team of software engineers to deliver high-impact results. Your responsibilities in this role:

• Own the reliability and timeliness of the real-time catalog feeds and publication pipeline that unblock every downstream, member-facing system, including the fast lanes and override lanes that keep a bad entry from holding up the rest of the catalog

• Own Catalog Entity, our shared content modeling abstraction, evolving it to represent common structure and content-type-specific variation across films, episodic series, live shows, sports, and future content types without requiring a bespoke pipeline for each

• Own the data integrity of the catalog: validate collected data against the model and business logic, hold back or override bad changes, and detect and remediate systemic feed failures

• Partner with peer teams on setup-side object modeling and on the downstream member-facing contract

• Lead collaboration with engineers, program managers, product managers, and other stakeholders to drive vision, strategy, and adoption

• Foster a culture of accountability, ensuring timely and reliable delivery of the team's roadmap to support business needs

• Act as a trusted technical advisor, guiding thoughtful decision-making in ambiguous situations

• Communicate complex ideas clearly and influence decisions among diverse stakeholders

• Balance business goals with strong engineering practices, investing in foundational work and continuous improvements

• Hire, coach, and lead a team of engineers with deep data modeling and distributed systems expertise, inspiring exceptional results in stability, performance, and product experience

• Build an inclusive team culture where everyone feels empowered, accepted, and respected

What we are looking for

• 3 or more years building and managing high-performing, inclusive teams, attracting top talent, fostering accountability, and ensuring all voices inform decisions.

• Experience delivering and operating high-performance data pipelines with near-real-time latency, balanced with consistency and partition tolerance, behind production internet consumer-scale workloads

• Experience driving a culture of excellence, unlocking high-velocity business and product results while cultivating an ownership culture with best-in-breed systems reliability and operational readiness.

• Proven ability to define and communicate systems strategy to drive long-term product feature enablement.

• Skilled at prioritizing team efforts, aligning them with business objectives, and using data, input, and pilot investments to bring rigor to decision-making.

• Effective communication and collaboration skills to build cross-functional partnerships, influence strategic direction, and empower team members across global teams.

Nice to have

• Experience building generative AI solutions in ambiguous environments, with a proven ability to creatively experiment, develop innovative approaches, and collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams.

• Experience leading engineering teams supporting large-scale data pipelines updating in the 10M+ updates/second regime

• Experience with in-memory data snapshot architectures, point-in-time consistency, or graph-aware rollback/recovery systems

• Experience leading the operation and optimization of CPU- and memory-intensive cloud services in the range of 1,000s to 10,000s of CPUss
